checks.name: a5-scheduler-checked-before-the-owner-map
checks.summary: A5 MEASURED. internal/api/CombinedAuthenticator gains exactly one field, SchedulerIdentity string. Authenticate's order is unchanged where it matters and the new branch sits in exactly one place: (1) the runner-session header branch, BYTE-UNCHANGED (verified by `git diff` over auth.go, which touches only the struct declaration and the block between parseIAPEmail and the OwnerEmails lookup); (2) parseIAPEmail; (3) NEW -- if the trimmed lowercased SchedulerIdentity is non-empty, refuse an overlap with OwnerEmails, then return application.LoopCaller(email) when it equals the asserted email; (4) the existing OwnerEmails lookup and RoleOwner return, unchanged. Checking BEFORE the owner map is load-bearing, not stylistic: an identity that resolved as owner first would silently acquire every owner-only route. ASSERTED, executed: the same authenticator resolves the scheduler address to RoleScheduler with the asserted email as Subject and an empty RunnerID, resolves the allowlisted owner to RoleOwner, refuses a stranger, folds case on both sides (an upper-case assertion of the scheduler address still resolves, and the Subject is the normalised lowercase form, which is what makes it usable as a domain ActorID), and -- with the field left empty -- behaves exactly as it did at a0622910d493cadd94c6d819690dbab0232a44ab: the scheduler's own address is simply not an owner and is refused. Verdict: '--- PASS: TestCombinedAuthenticatorResolvesTheSchedulerBeforeTheOwnerMap'.

checks.name: a5-a6-an-identity-configured-as-both-is-refused
checks.summary: A5's and A6's REFUSAL PROOF, executed. An email present in BOTH OwnerEmails and SchedulerIdentity makes Authenticate return an ERROR naming the misconfiguration -- 'misconfigured identity: the scheduler identity is also an owner email; an asserted identity must have exactly one role' -- and never a Caller: the test asserts, for the overlapping address AND for the separate owner address AND for a stranger, that err is non-nil, that the returned Caller is the zero value, and that the message contains 'scheduler identity is also an owner email'. The refusal is deliberately UNCONDITIONAL on the asserted identity rather than scoped to the overlapping one, because a deployment in that state has no defensible answer for any IAP caller; it is not resolved by precedence, because a single asserted email must produce exactly one role or an error. Case folding and padding do not let the overlap slip through: SchedulerIdentity '  RECONCILER@Example.IAM.gserviceaccount.COM  ' against an OwnerEmails entry of the lowercase form is refused too. Verdict: '--- PASS: TestCombinedAuthenticatorRefusesAnIdentityConfiguredAsBothSchedulerAndOwner'.

checks.name: a6-no-start-time-refusal-was-added-UNMET
checks.summary: A6, THE UNMET HALF, recorded as failed and escalated to the tech_lead rather than reinterpreted, weakened or written as a pass. A6 asks for THREE things that cannot all hold: (i) 'If RECONCILE_IDENTITY also appears in OWNER_EMAILS the process must fail to start with a message naming the conflict'; (ii) 'Add NO new environment variable and change nothing else in that file'; (iii) 'assert that by unit-testing the authenticator's refusal, since cmd/control-plane has no test package'. (i) can only be satisfied by a second added guard in cmd/control-plane/main.go's run(), which (ii) forbids, and which would be an UNTESTED guard because (iii) states the package has no test target -- and an untested guard is not a guard. WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD: the refusal lives in CombinedAuthenticator.Authenticate, where it is asserted by TestCombinedAuthenticatorRefusesAnIdentityConfiguredAsBothSchedulerAndOwner for the overlapping address, for the separate owner address and for a stranger, with the message naming the misconfiguration and the returned Caller being the zero value in every case. WHAT IS THEREFORE NOT TRUE: a control-plane process configured with RECONCILE_IDENTITY inside OWNER_EMAILS still STARTS. It then refuses every IAP-authenticated request, so it is fail-closed at the request boundary and not at startup, and an operator sees the conflict named in every 401 rather than once on stderr. checks.name: a9-the-executed-proof-over-the-composed-handler
checks.summary: A9, executed over the composed HTTP handler with a REAL api.CombinedAuthenticator -- not a bearer map -- configured with an owner email, a DIFFERENT scheduler email, and the scheduler email as ReconcileIdentity, which is exactly how cmd/control-plane wires it. (a) ATTRIBUTION, the centre: POST /v1/requirements asserting the scheduler identity returns 201; the response's requested_by reads actor_type 'loop' with the asserted identity as subject; the STORED domain.Requirement read straight out of the memory store has RequestedBy.ActorType == domain.ActorTypeLoop and RequestedBy.Subject == the scheduler identity; the same capture as the owner reads 'owner' in the response and domain.ActorTypeOwner in the store. GET /v1/requirements/{id} reports the same for both, read AS THE OWNER because that route is owner-only (api.go:194, an unchanged gate) -- the point being that the value the Loop wrote is what the owner sees -- and the scheduler is 403 on that read. (b) POST /v1/requirements/{id}:start-framing as the scheduler returns 200, the stored Requirement moves to domain.RequirementFraming, and its RequestedBy still reads loop after the transition. (c) POST /v1/requirements/{id}:request-input as the scheduler returns 200. (d) POST /v1/repositories as the scheduler returns 403 and POST /v1/requirements/{id}:answer-input as the scheduler returns 403 -- both owner-only at the transport, and both refused before any command runs. (e) POST /internal/reconcile with the OWNER identity returns 401 and the hook never runs; with the SCHEDULER identity it returns 202, the hook runs exactly once, and application.CallerFromContext on the context it was handed returns RoleScheduler with the reconcile identity as Subject -- so the carried caller is verified as present and correctly attributed. checks.name: a14-determinism-and-quota
checks.summary: A14 MEASURED over every new and modified test. No new or modified test contains time.Sleep, time.After, time.NewTimer, time.Tick, time.Now, `go ` (a goroutine), math/rand or crypto/rand: verified by grepping the four touched test files for each of those tokens. Every clock is injected: internal/api's new fixture uses framingClock, the steppable injected clock the V2-082 chain test already introduced, advanced only by its own nextDay() method; internal/runner's new tests reuse the package's existing journeyClock, which returns a fixed time.Unix(1700000000, 0).UTC(); internal/application's new tests use the package's existing service() helper and its fixed clock. There is no wait of any kind in any new test, so there is no deadline poll to bound and no measured duration is asserted as a threshold. The whole suite was run with -race and -count=1 and reported ok for every package. QUOTA: the in-memory adapter does not true up its quota reservation, so quota.ReadTransactionUsage (Reads 6001, Writes 1, at internal/quota/quota.go:56) admits only FOUR read transactions per budget day against quota.DefaultBudget's 25000 reads (internal/quota/quota.go:46). The A9 proof performs three GET /v1/requirements/{id} reads plus three captures plus two verb mutations plus two 403s plus five reconcile requests, so the injected clock is stepped a whole UTC day three times (after the captures, before the two verbs, and before the owner-only refusals) rather than dropping a read or weakening an assertion. internal/quota is prohibited and that adapter defect stays V2-087's. ONE deliberate residual randomness, recorded rather than hidden: internal/api/auth_test.go's runner-session test drives the real enrollment protocol, whose nonce and tokens come from crypto/rand inside internal/runner's PRODUCTION code (the pre-existing TestRunnerEnrollmentHTTPChallengeFlow does the same); the test itself introduces none -- its ed25519 key is derived from an all-zero seed rather than generated -- and no assertion depends on any random value.
